 All students are expected to maintain a respectful, responsible, and professional
 demeanor at all times. The following principles apply to both online and onsite

 CONDUCT PRINCIPLES 
 
 
 Show respect for instructors, staff, fellow students, and all ITI personnel.

 learning environment or tarnishes our values. 
 
 
 DRESS CODE 
 
 
 Students must present themselves in a manner appropriate for a professional
 training environment. This applies during both in-person attendance and
 online sessions: 
 
 Wear clean, modest, and tidy attire at all times. 
 Closed-toed shoes are mandatory onsite. 
 Avoid shorts, ripped jeans, slippers, flip-flops, or beachwear.

 Hair should be neat and grooming should align with Egyptian workplace
 norms. 
 Face coverings (such as niqabs, masks, or caps) must be removed during
 
 exams, assessments, or identification processes for security purposes.
 
 Note: If a student’s attire is deemed inappropriate, Student Affairs reserves
 the right to issue a verbal or written warning and require a change of
 dress.

 ASSESSMENT & GRADING 
 
 
 Understanding how your performance is assessed is the key to your success at ITI.
 
 This section outlines how assignments, exams, and overall progress are evaluated
 throughout the program.

 online. 
 
 
 
 ASSIGNMENTS All assignments must follow provided instructions. Late
 submissions are penalized with a 5-point deduction per
 day unless an extension is granted in advance. 
 
 
 
 EXAMS A minimum of 60% is required to pass any course.
 Some tracks may use cumulative assessments. Late
 arrival up to 20% of exam time is allowed with penalty;
 more than that, the student loses the right to take the
 exam. One corrective exam may be granted at the
 discretion of the Academic Supervisor. 
 
 
 CORRECTIVE EXAMS Only one opportunity is granted for a corrective exam
 
 per subject, subject to Academic Affairs approval.
